rounds.text: The business is experiencing a powerful fundamental acceleration, evidenced by a 20% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months and a dramatic 277% compounded profit growth over the same period [E17, E21]. This operational momentum is supported by an expanding operating margin of 18% in the TTM, representing a 4 percentage point improvement over three years [E30]. Market participants are recognizing this sharp inflection, driving a 125% compounded share price growth over the past year and achieving a top-tier relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 [E25, E49]. Furthermore, results score 84 out of 100 with net profit up 108% year-over-year, signaling that the company is starting to outperform expectations and breaking past historical stagnation [E55, E72]. Conceded: [E1] and [E43].

Lokesh Machines Ltd carries extreme valuation and fundamental risks that are completely disconnected from its current market price of ₹ 362 [E2]. The stock trades at an exorbitant P/E ratio of 155x compared to a sector benchmark of just 21.26x, alongside an EV/EBITDA of 21.99x that heavily outpaces the sector's 12.25x [E1, E6, E11]. This expensive pricing is underpinned by deeply depressed returns on capital, with a meager ROE of 1.86% and ROCE of 5.68%, both trailing sector benchmarks by wide margins [E9, E10]. Furthermore, fundamental value is severely compromised by negative cash generation, evidenced by operating cash flow dropping to Rs -13 Cr and free cash flow sinking to Rs -29 Cr in March 2026 [E35, E36]. The disconnect between price and reality is laid bare by a discounted cash flow intrinsic value of Rs 25, resulting in an eye-watering margin of safety of -1334.5% and a reverse DCF implying an unrealistic 37.3% earnings growth [E43, E44, E45]. Finally, insider confidence is eroding as promoter holdings have declined to 49.17% in September 2026 from 52.40% in December 2023, accompanied by a staggering historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -93.5% and high annualized volatility of 57.2% [E40, E51, E52]. conceded: [E17], [E21], [E30], [E49], [E50], [E64], [E65], [E66], [E67].

Conceded: [E1], [E6], [E11], [E9], [E10], [E35], [E36], [E43], [E44], [E45], [E40], [E51], [E52]. While the bear focuses on these static ratios and historical headwinds, it dismisses the powerful operational inflection currently underway, evidenced by a 20% surge in trailing twelve-month sales growth and a massive 277% compounded profit growth over the same period [E17, E21]. This dramatic fundamental acceleration is why the stock commands a maximum relative-strength rating of 100 against the Nifty 500 and an 88% twelve-month price return [E49, E50]. Furthermore, operating margins have expanded by 4 percentage points compared to three years earlier, sitting at 18% in the TTM period [E30]. The rules-based screen explicitly highlights these strengths with a score of 71 out of 100, driven by soaring YoY sales and net profit growth [E63, E64, E66]. Dismissing these active operational metrics as mere "stale sentiment" ignores the reality that results are improving with an 84/100 results score, proving the business is successfully turning around [E72].

Conceded: [E17], [E21], [E64], [E66]. While the bull points to recent momentum in sales and profit growth, this short-term acceleration masks a severe longer-term decay, including a 3-year compounded sales growth of -4% and a 3-year profit contraction of -23% [E16, E20]. The claim of an operational inflection ignores that the quarterly operating margin has actually slipped by 2 percentage points to 17% in Sep 2026 compared to the year-ago quarter, with overall yearly and quarterly margin trends remaining inconsistent [E31, E32, E33]. Furthermore, relying on a rules-based score of 71 overlooks the scanX engine's direct warnings that earnings growth is decelerating and that the stock is severely overvalued in a DCF framework [E68, E70]. The relative-strength rating of 100 and price returns are completely detached from fundamentals, particularly when the company generated negative operating cash flow of Rs -13 Cr and negative free cash flow of Rs -29 Cr in Mar 2026 [E35, E36, E50]. Finally, dismissing valuation concerns as stale sentiment is a dangerous oversight given that a reverse DCF dictates the price already aggressively prices in 37.3% earnings growth while carrying a low median ROE of just 3% over the last three years [E28, E45, E72].
